laws.title: Hands-Free Driving Law
laws.subtitle: HI Code §291C-137 — No handheld devices while driving
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii prohibits holding or using handheld electronic devices while driving. Handheld device use while driving is banned.
laws.penalty: $150 first, $200 second, $300 third+.
laws.exceptions: Emergency 911 calls are exempt from hands-free requirements.

quiz.q: Is handheld phone use banned while driving in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: all handheld electronic device use while driving is banned.

laws.title: Non-Resident Hunting & Fishing License
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §183D-22 — Non-residents must purchase licenses
laws.fullDescription: Non-residents must obtain a valid Hawaii hunting or fishing license before taking game or fish. Annual non-resident fishing licenses cost approximately $26; hunting licenses cost approximately $95. Some species require additional tags.
laws.penalty: Class B misdemeanor or felony; fines up to $2000 plus equipment forfeiture.
laws.exceptions: Residents are exempt from non-resident fees.

quiz.q: What is the penalty for hunting without a license in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hunting without a license in Hawaii is a Class B misdemeanor with fines up to $2000.

laws.title: Impaired Driving (DUI/DWI)
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §291E-61 — 0.08% BAC limit
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii prohibits operating a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. Commercial drivers: 0.04%. Drivers under 21: 0.02 BAC. Implied consent laws apply.
laws.penalty: First offense: $250–$1,000 fine, 90-day license revocation, up to 5 days jail (first offense). Subsequent offenses carry mandatory minimums and longer suspensions.
laws.exceptions: None — even prescription medication impairment can result in DUI charges.

quiz.q: What BAC triggers a DUI in Hawaii for regular drivers?
quiz.explanation: The legal BAC limit in Hawaii is 0.08% for regular drivers, consistent with all US states.

laws.title: Open Container Law
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §291-3.3 — No open alcohol in vehicles
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii prohibits open alcoholic beverage containers in the passenger area of motor vehicles on public roads. Open container law applies to driver and passengers.
laws.penalty: $250 fine; applies to driver and passengers.
laws.exceptions: Passengers in for-hire vehicles (taxis, limos) may be exempt.

quiz.q: Can passengers drink alcohol in a private car in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii's open container law applies to all vehicle occupants.

laws.title: Recreational Cannabis — Legal
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §329D — Recreational cannabis legal — adults 21+ (retail 2025)
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Hawaii legalized adult-use cannabis in 2023 (SB 669). Adults 21+ may possess up to 1 oz. Home cultivation of 3 plants is allowed. Retail dispensary sales are scheduled to begin 2025.
laws.penalty: Public consumption: $130 fine.
laws.exceptions: Medical patients exempt.

quiz.q: Is recreational cannabis legal in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii legalized recreational cannabis in 2023; retail sales begin 2025.

laws.title: Medical Cannabis — Legal
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §329-121 — Medical cannabis program
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii has had a medical cannabis program since 2000 (first state to legalize via legislature, not ballot). Patients may possess up to 4 oz.
laws.penalty: Non-patients face criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Registered patients are exempt from possession penalties.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have a medical cannabis program?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii has a medical cannabis program.

laws.title: Firearm Carry Law — Shall-issue
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §134-9 — Shall-issue state
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii is a shall-issue state. Hawaii changed from may-issue to shall-issue after the 2022 Bruen ruling. A permit is required to carry concealed. Hawaii still maintains strict permitting requirements.
laws.penalty: Carrying while prohibited: felony.
laws.exceptions: Firearms prohibited in schools, courts, and government buildings.

quiz.q: What type of carry law does Hawaii have?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii has shall-issue — concealed carry requires a permit; Hawaii moved to shall-issue after the 2022 Bruen ruling

laws.title: Background Check Requirements
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §18 USC 922 — Federal NICS checks at licensed dealers
laws.fullDescription: All firearm purchases from licensed dealers in Hawaii require a federal NICS background check. Hawaii requires background checks and registration for all firearm acquisitions, including private sales. Hawaii is one of the most restrictive gun states.
laws.penalty: Straw purchases or sales to prohibited persons: federal felony up to 10 years.
laws.exceptions: Transfers between immediate family members may be exempt.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii require background checks for private gun sales?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii requires background checks for all gun sales.

laws.title: Stand Your Ground / Castle Doctrine
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Criminal Code — Castle Doctrine only
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii has a Castle Doctrine but no Stand Your Ground law. There is a duty to retreat outside the home before using deadly force.
laws.penalty: N/A — this law provides a defense against criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Force not justified if defender is committing a crime or the intruder is a co-resident.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have a Stand Your Ground law?
options: No — duty to retreat outside home
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Hawaii has Castle Doctrine in the home but duty to retreat exists outside.

laws.title: Minimum Wage Law
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Labor Code — $14.00/hour minimum wage
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii's minimum wage is $14.00/hour (2024). Hawaii's minimum wage is $14.00/hr (2024), rising to $18/hr by 2028 under a phased increase passed in 2022.
laws.penalty: Employers violating minimum wage: back wages, double damages, and attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Tipped workers may have a lower base wage.

quiz.q: What is the minimum wage in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii's minimum wage is $14.00/hour.

laws.title: At-Will Employment
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Labor Code — Employment at will doctrine
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii follows at-will employment. Employers may terminate for any legal reason; employees may quit anytime. at-will employment with standard exceptions.
laws.penalty: N/A — at-will is the default standard.
laws.exceptions: Termination for illegal reasons (discrimination, retaliation) is prohibited.

quiz.q: Can an Hawaii employer fire an employee without giving a reason?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii is an at-will employment state — employers may generally terminate without cause.

laws.title: Right-to-Work Law — No
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Labor Code — Hawaii is NOT a right-to-work state
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii is not a right-to-work state. Hawaii is not a right-to-work state.
laws.penalty: N/A — this governs labor relations framework.
laws.exceptions: Federal employees and some categories are governed by federal law.

quiz.q: Is Hawaii a right-to-work state?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii is NOT a right-to-work state.

laws.title: Non-Compete Agreement Enforceability
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Business Code — Non-compete enforceability rules
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Non-compete agreements enforced if reasonable in scope and duration.
laws.penalty: Overly broad agreements may be voided or reformed by courts.
laws.exceptions: Agreements protecting legitimate trade secrets are most favored.

quiz.q: Are non-compete agreements automatically enforceable in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Courts assess reasonableness of non-competes.

laws.title: Paid Sick Leave — Required
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §392-21 — Paid sick leave through temporary disability insurance
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Hawaii requires employers to provide temporary disability insurance (TDI), covering a portion of wages during illness or injury. It also requires family leave under the Hawaii Family Leave Law.
laws.penalty: Violation: civil fines.
laws.exceptions: Independent contractors are generally not covered.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii require employers to provide paid sick leave?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Hawaii requires temporary disability insurance and family leave coverage.

laws.title: Unemployment Insurance
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Labor Code — Unemployment benefits
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii unemployment insurance provides benefits to eligible workers. Maximum weekly benefit: $799 for up to 26 weeks. Workers must have earned at least $1500 in the base period.
laws.penalty: Filing fraudulent claims: repayment plus penalties and possible criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Self-employed and independent contractors are generally ineligible for regular UI.

quiz.q: What is the maximum weekly unemployment benefit in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii's maximum weekly unemployment benefit is $799.

laws.title: Workers' Compensation
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Labor Code — Mandatory workers' comp coverage
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii requires employers with 1 or more employees to carry workers' compensation insurance. Covers medical costs and lost wages for work-related injuries.
laws.penalty: Employers without coverage: fines up to $5000/day, personal liability for claims.
laws.exceptions: Sole proprietors and some domestic workers may be exempt.

quiz.q: How many employees trigger workers' comp requirements in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii requires workers' comp for employers with 1 or more employees.

laws.title: Independent Contractor Classification
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Labor Code — Worker classification rules
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii uses Common law control test to classify workers. Worker classification uses the common law control test.
laws.penalty: Misclassification: back taxes, penalties, and retroactive benefits liability.
laws.exceptions: Licensed professionals may have different classification standards.

quiz.q: What test does Hawaii use for worker classification?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii uses the Common law control test for worker classification.

laws.title: Child Labor Laws
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Labor Code — Restrictions on youth employment
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii restricts employment of minors. Children under 14: very limited jobs only. Ages 14–15: restricted hours. Most minors under 18 need work permits. Federal child labor protections apply with state additions.
laws.penalty: Employers violating child labor laws: fines up to $10000 per violation.
laws.exceptions: Family farms and limited entertainment work have exemptions.

quiz.q: At what age do minors generally need work permits in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Most Hawaii minors under 18 need work permits for regular employment.

laws.title: Equal Pay Act
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Civil Rights Code — Equal pay for equal work
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii prohibits pay discrimination based on sex for substantially equal work. Equal pay laws prohibit sex-based wage discrimination.
laws.penalty: Back pay, compensatory damages, and attorney fees for violations.
laws.exceptions: Pay differences justified by seniority, merit, or non-sex factors are permitted.

quiz.q: What agency enforces equal pay laws in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii's civil rights agency and the federal EEOC both enforce equal pay laws.

laws.title: Anti-Discrimination in Employment
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §378-2 — Protected classes in Hawaii
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii prohibits employment discrimination based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, and HIV/AIDS status. Hawaii has one of the broadest anti-discrimination laws, covering sexual orientation since 1991.
laws.penalty: Compensatory damages, back pay, reinstatement, and attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Religious organizations may have limited exemptions for certain positions.

quiz.q: How many employees must an Hawaii employer have before anti-discrimination laws apply?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii anti-discrimination laws apply to employers with 1 or more employees.

laws.title: Landlord Entry Notice Requirement
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Landlord-Tenant Act — 24-hour notice required
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii landlords must give tenants 24 hours' written notice before entering for non-emergency purposes. Entry must be at reasonable times.
laws.penalty: Unlawful entry may entitle tenant to damages or lease termination.
laws.exceptions: Emergencies (fire, flood, imminent harm) allow immediate entry without notice.

quiz.q: How many hours notice must Hawaii landlords give before entering?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii landlords must give 24 hours' notice before non-emergency entry.

laws.title: Security Deposit Rules
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Landlord-Tenant Act — Two months' rent maximum deposit
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Maximum security deposit is Two months' rent. Deposits must be returned within 30 days of move-out with an itemized statement of deductions.
laws.penalty: Landlord who wrongfully withholds deposit may owe double damages plus attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Deposits for pets may be separate in some cases.

quiz.q: How many days does a Hawaii landlord have to return a security deposit?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii landlords have 30 days to return security deposits after move-out.

laws.title: Rent Control Status — Not Statewide
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Housing Code — No statewide rent control
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Hawaii has no statewide rent control, though high housing costs have driven persistent calls for it.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a policy/regulatory matter.
laws.exceptions: Federally subsidized housing has separate rent rules.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have statewide rent control?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Hawaii has no statewide rent control.

laws.title: Eviction Process & Tenant Protections
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Landlord-Tenant Act — Notice and court process required
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii landlords must provide: 5 days notice for nonpayment; 10 days for violations; 30 days for no-cause termination. Court filing required after notice expires.
laws.penalty: Self-help eviction (changing locks, removing belongings) is illegal.
laws.exceptions: Emergency situations may allow expedited proceedings.

quiz.q: How many days notice for non-payment of rent before eviction in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii requires 5 days notice for nonpayment of rent before filing for eviction.

laws.title: Short-Term Rental (STR) Regulations
laws.subtitle: Local codes — Regulated locally
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: STR regulations vary by municipality.
laws.penalty: Operating without required licenses: fines and possible closure.
laws.exceptions: Owner-occupied properties renting a single room may have reduced requirements.

quiz.q: Are short-term rentals (Airbnb) regulated in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii regulates STRs primarily at the local level with varying requirements by city.

laws.title: Property Tax
laws.subtitle: Local codes — Average 0.27% effective rate
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Average effective property tax rate is approximately 0.27%. Hawaii has the lowest effective property tax rate in the US, but home values are very high, so dollar amounts are still significant.
laws.penalty: Delinquent taxes accrue interest and may result in tax lien or foreclosure.
laws.exceptions: Senior citizens and disabled veterans often receive exemptions. Senior and veteran exemptions available.

quiz.q: What is the approximate average effective property tax rate in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii's average effective property tax rate is approximately 0.27%.

laws.title: Homestead Exemption
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §246-29 — $100,000 assessed value exemption homestead exemption
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Hawaii's homestead exemption reduces the assessed value by $100,000 for owner-occupied primary residences.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a protection for homeowners.
laws.exceptions: Does not protect against tax liens, mortgage foreclosures, or mechanic's liens.

quiz.q: What is Hawaii's homestead exemption?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii's homestead exemption is $100,000 assessed value exemption.

laws.title: State Income Tax — Yes — graduated up to 11%
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §235-51 — Yes — graduated up to 11%
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Hawaii has one of the highest top income tax rates in the US at 11%, with rates ranging from 1.4% to 11%.
laws.penalty: Tax evasion: civil penalties, back taxes, and possible criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Federal income taxes apply to all residents regardless of state income tax.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have a state income tax?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Hawaii has graduated income tax with a top rate of 11% — one of the highest in the US.

laws.title: Sales Tax Rate
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Revenue Code — 4.0% statewide sales tax
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii has a 4.0% statewide sales tax. Hawaii's General Excise Tax (GET) of 4% functions like a sales tax but applies to all business transactions. Effectively 4.5% with county surcharge in Honolulu. Combined state and local rates average 4.5%.
laws.penalty: Tax evasion: civil penalties and criminal charges for substantial violations.
laws.exceptions: Exempt items typically include: Some medical services are exempt..

quiz.q: What is the statewide sales tax rate in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii's statewide sales tax is 4.0%.

laws.title: Estate / Inheritance Tax — Yes
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §236E — Yes — estate tax on estates over $5.49M
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Hawaii imposes a state estate tax on estates over $5.49 million (2024), with rates up to 20% — one of the highest state estate tax rates.
laws.penalty: N/A — federal estate tax applies to all US residents with large estates.
laws.exceptions: Federal estate tax applies to estates over $13 million (2024).

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have a state estate or inheritance tax?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Hawaii imposes an estate tax with rates up to 20% on large estates.

laws.title: Smoke-Free Workplace Law
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Health Code — Clean Air Act / Smoke-Free law
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii prohibits smoking in enclosed workplaces, restaurants, and bars.
laws.penalty: Violation: $100–$500 per incident for individuals.
laws.exceptions: Some private clubs and outdoor areas may be exempt.

quiz.q: Is smoking banned in workplaces and restaurants in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Comprehensive smoke-free law covers most indoor workplaces.

laws.title: Motorcycle Helmet Law
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Vehicle Code — Universal helmet law
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: All motorcycle riders must wear helmets.
laws.penalty: Helmet violation: $100 fine.
laws.exceptions: N/A

quiz.q: Who must wear a motorcycle helmet in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Universal helmet law.

laws.title: Seatbelt Law
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Vehicle Code — Mandatory seatbelts
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii requires all front-seat occupants to wear seatbelts. Children under 8 or under 60 lbs must be in child safety seats.
laws.penalty: $25 fine for violations; higher for child restraint violations.
laws.exceptions: Some commercial vehicles and emergency situations may have limited exemptions.

quiz.q: Is the seatbelt law a primary offense in Hawaii?
options: Yes, police can stop for seatbelt alone
quiz.explanation: Hawaii's seatbelt law is a primary enforcement offense.

laws.title: Speed Limits
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Vehicle Code — Statutory speed limits
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Residential: 25 mph; highways: 55 mph; interstates: 60 mph; school zones: 20 mph. Hawaii has lower speed limits than most states due to its terrain and population density.
laws.penalty: Speeding fines start at $50 and increase with severity; reckless driving is a criminal charge.
laws.exceptions: Emergency vehicles are exempt when responding.

quiz.q: What is the interstate speed limit in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii's standard interstate speed limit is 60 mph.

laws.title: Texting While Driving
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Vehicle Code — Texting while driving banned
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Texting while driving is prohibited.
laws.penalty: First offense: $150; repeat: $200.
laws.exceptions: Emergency 911 calls are permitted while driving.

quiz.q: Is texting while driving banned in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Hawaii bans all handheld electronic device use while driving.

laws.title: DUI Checkpoint Legality
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Vehicle Code — Sobriety checkpoints permitted
laws.fullDescription: DUI sobriety checkpoints are legal in Hawaii. DUI checkpoints legal with proper procedures.
laws.penalty: N/A — this defines when checkpoints are legal.
laws.exceptions: Checkpoints must follow established procedures to be constitutional.

quiz.q: Are DUI sobriety checkpoints legal in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: DUI checkpoints are legal with proper procedures.

laws.title: Move Over Law
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Vehicle Code — Slow or move over for emergency vehicles
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii's Move Over Law requires drivers to change lanes or slow down when passing stopped emergency vehicles and tow trucks and highway maintenance vehicles with flashing lights on the roadway or shoulder.
laws.penalty: Violation: $250 fine; if injury or death results, criminal charges may apply.
laws.exceptions: Required only when safe to do so without creating greater hazard.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii's Move Over Law cover tow trucks?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii's Move Over Law covers tow trucks.

laws.title: Cell Phone Use While Driving
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §291C-137 — Handheld device restrictions
laws.fullDescription: Beyond texting, Hawaii restricts handheld phone use while driving.
laws.penalty: Fines range from $150 to $200.
laws.exceptions: Hands-free calls and navigation use are generally permitted.

quiz.q: Can drivers make calls on a handheld phone while driving in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Handheld phone restrictions apply while driving.

laws.title: Age of Majority
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Civil Code — Age 18 is legal adulthood
laws.fullDescription: In Hawaii, the age of majority is 18. At 18, residents gain the right to vote, enter contracts, and make their own legal decisions. Age-specific restrictions still apply.
laws.penalty: N/A — this defines civil rights.
laws.exceptions: Some rights have higher age thresholds: alcohol (21), cannabis where legal (21).

quiz.q: What is the age of majority in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii's age of majority is 18, consistent with most US states.

laws.title: Voting Rights & Restoration
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Election Code — Voter eligibility and felon restoration
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Felons lose voting rights during incarceration; restoration rules vary by state.
laws.penalty: Voting while ineligible (while incarcerated): criminal charge.
laws.exceptions: Mentally incapacitated persons adjudicated incompetent may lose voting rights.

quiz.q: When are voting rights restored to a felon in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Voting rights restored after completing sentence.

laws.title: Jury Duty Requirements
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Court Rules — Jury service
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii citizens who are US citizens, 18+, registered voters (or driver's license holders) may be called for jury duty. Jurors receive $50/day. Employers must allow employees to serve.
laws.penalty: Willfully ignoring a jury summons: contempt of court, fines up to $500.
laws.exceptions: Exemptions include active military, police, extreme hardship, and some medical conditions.

quiz.q: What is the daily pay for jurors in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii jurors receive $50 per day for service.

laws.title: Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Child Welfare Act — Mandatory reporters
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Designated professionals are mandatory reporters. Reports must be made to child protective services or law enforcement. Good-faith reporters are protected from liability.
laws.penalty: Failure to report known child abuse: misdemeanor.
laws.exceptions: Attorney-client privilege may apply in limited circumstances.

quiz.q: Who must report suspected child abuse in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Designated professionals must report suspected child abuse.

laws.title: Age of Consent
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Criminal Code — Age of consent is 16
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii's age of consent is 16. Sexual activity with persons under the age of consent is a criminal offense. Sex offenders must register with the state registry.
laws.penalty: Sexual abuse of a minor: Felony with sex offender registration..
laws.exceptions: Romeo and Juliet provision: Romeo and Juliet provision may apply for close-in-age couples..

quiz.q: What is the age of consent in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii's age of consent is 16.

laws.title: Emancipation of Minors
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Family Code — Court-ordered emancipation
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii allows minors aged 16+ to petition for emancipation, granting adult legal status. The court considers whether it's in the minor's best interests and whether the minor can support themselves.
laws.penalty: N/A — emancipation is a civil court process.
laws.exceptions: Emancipation does not override minimum age laws for alcohol, cannabis, or voting.

quiz.q: At what minimum age can a minor petition for emancipation in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii allows minors aged 16+ to petition for emancipation.

laws.title: Curfew Laws for Minors
laws.subtitle: Local codes — Local ordinances only
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: No statewide curfew; municipalities set their own rules.
laws.penalty: Curfew violation: minor taken into custody and released to parents; parents may face fines.
laws.exceptions: Minors with employment, parental supervision, or school activities are typically exempt.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have a statewide youth curfew?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Curfews set locally.

laws.title: Corporal Punishment in Schools
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Education Code — Corporal punishment prohibited
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Corporal punishment is prohibited in all Hawaii public schools.
laws.penalty: Educators using prohibited corporal punishment face administrative discipline and potential criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Physical restraint to prevent imminent harm is permitted.

quiz.q: Is corporal punishment allowed in Hawaii public schools?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Corporal punishment prohibited in public schools.

laws.title: Homeschooling Regulations
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Education Code — Homeschooling requirements
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Families must notify the school district and cover required subjects.
laws.penalty: Failure to provide required education: mandatory enrollment in public school.
laws.exceptions: Some states have additional oversight or assessment requirements.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have strict homeschooling regulations?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii has moderate-regulation homeschooling with moderate requirements with notification and required subjects.

laws.title: School Vaccination Requirements
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Health Code — Required vaccinations for school entry
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii requires students to be vaccinated against standard childhood diseases for school entry. Standard vaccinations required for school entry.
laws.penalty: Unvaccinated students without exemptions may be excluded from school.
laws.exceptions: Exemptions available: medical and religious exemptions.

quiz.q: Can Hawaii parents claim a philosophical exemption from school vaccinations?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii vaccination exemptions: medical and religious exemptions.

laws.title: Abortion Laws
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §453-16 — Legal — no restrictions under state law
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Abortion is legal in Hawaii with no gestational limits under state law. Hawaii was one of the first states to legalize abortion (1970) before Roe v. Wade.
laws.penalty: N/A — abortion is fully protected.
laws.exceptions: Medical emergencies to save the life of the mother are typically exempt.

quiz.q: What is the gestational limit on abortion in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Hawaii legalized abortion in 1970 before Roe and has no gestational limit under state law.

laws.title: Death Penalty — Abolished
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §706-656 — Death penalty status
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii does not have the death penalty. Hawaii abolished the death penalty in 1957, making it the first US territory to do so before statehood.
laws.penalty: Maximum punishment is life without parole.
laws.exceptions: Federal death penalty may apply to federal crimes regardless of state law.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have the death penalty?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Hawaii abolished the death penalty in 1957 before statehood.

laws.title: Medical Aid in Dying (MAID)
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §327L — Legal — Our Care Our Choice Act (2018)
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Hawaii enacted the Our Care Our Choice Act in 2018, allowing terminally ill adults with a 6-month prognosis to request life-ending medication.
laws.penalty: N/A — legal for eligible patients.
laws.exceptions: Withdrawal of life support and palliative sedation are legal with patient consent everywhere.

quiz.q: Is medical aid in dying (assisted suicide) legal in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Medical aid in dying is legal in Hawaii under the Our Care Our Choice Act (2018).

laws.title: Drug Penalties (Non-Cannabis)
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Controlled Substances Act — Controlled Substances Act
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii controlled substance penalties: Drug penalties follow state scheduling.
laws.penalty: Possession of hard drugs: misdemeanor to felony. Distribution/manufacture: felony up to 30 years.
laws.exceptions: Prescribed medications used as directed are exempt.

quiz.q: Is simple drug possession a felony in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Drug penalties vary by substance and amount.

laws.title: Asset Forfeiture Laws
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Criminal Code — Civil asset forfeiture
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Civil asset forfeiture permitted for drug crimes.
laws.penalty: N/A — forfeiture is an action against property.
laws.exceptions: Innocent owner defense available: property returned if owner proves no criminal connection.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii require a criminal conviction before forfeiture?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Civil forfeiture allowed without conviction.

laws.title: Expungement & Record Sealing
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Criminal Code — Expungement availability
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Record sealing or expungement available for eligible offenses.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a post-conviction relief process.
laws.exceptions: Serious felonies, sex offenses, and violent crimes generally cannot be expunged.

quiz.q: Can first-time non-violent offenders expunge their records in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Limited expungement available.

laws.title: Solitary Confinement Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Corrections Code — Restricted housing policies
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: DOC policies limit solitary confinement use.
laws.penalty: N/A — this governs prison administration.
laws.exceptions: Extremely dangerous inmates may face longer restricted housing.

quiz.q: Has Hawaii restricted the use of solitary confinement?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Limited reforms on solitary confinement.

laws.title: Private Prison Use
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Corrections Code — Private correctional facilities
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Some private facilities used.

laws.title: Police Body Camera Requirements

laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Body camera policies vary by department.

laws.exceptions: Individual agencies may have stricter policies than state law requires.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have a statewide body camera law?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Body camera policies vary by agency.

laws.title: Police Use-of-Force Policies
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Criminal Code — Justified use of force
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii law: deadly force justified only when necessary to prevent death or serious injury.
laws.penalty: Unjustified use of force: potential criminal charges and civil liability.
laws.exceptions: Force always subject to the reasonableness standard.

quiz.q: When may Hawaii officers use deadly force?
options: When reasonably necessary to prevent death or serious injury
quiz.explanation: Hawaii officers may use deadly force only when reasonably necessary to prevent death or serious injury.

laws.title: Red Flag Law (ERPO) — Yes
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §134-61 — Extreme Risk Protection Orders
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii has a Red Flag (ERPO) law. Hawaii has an Extreme Risk Gun Violence Protective Order law allowing courts to temporarily remove firearms from at-risk individuals.
laws.penalty: N/A — ERPO is a civil court order, not a criminal penalty.
laws.exceptions: Existing domestic violence protective orders may include firearm surrender in all states.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have a Red Flag (ERPO) law?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii has an Extreme Risk Protection Order law.

laws.title: Hate Crime Laws
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Criminal Code — Bias-motivated crime laws
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii has hate crime laws providing sentencing enhancements.
laws.penalty: Hate crime enhancement or separate charge: sentencing enhancement.
laws.exceptions: Protected speech expressing bias without accompanying criminal conduct is constitutionally protected.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have hate crime laws?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Hate crime sentencing enhancements apply.

laws.title: Domestic Violence Laws & Protections
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Domestic Violence Act — Domestic Violence Act
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Comprehensive domestic violence protections including protective orders.
laws.penalty: Violation of DV protective order: misdemeanor to felony..
laws.exceptions: Mutual protective orders may be issued in some circumstances.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have mandatory arrest policies for domestic violence?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Protective orders and DV protections available.

laws.title: Stalking & Cyberstalking Laws
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Criminal Code — Stalking prohibition
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii prohibits stalking — repeated non-consensual contact causing substantial distress. Stalking prohibits repeated unwanted contact causing distress. Cyberstalking covered.
laws.penalty: First-degree stalking: felony. Second-degree: misdemeanor.
laws.exceptions: Lawful investigations by law enforcement are not considered stalking.

quiz.q: Is cyberstalking (electronic harassment) covered by Hawaii's stalking law?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii's stalking law covers cyberstalking through electronic means.

laws.title: Consumer Data Privacy Law
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Privacy Act — Data breach notification law
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Hawaii has a data breach notification law but is working toward a more comprehensive privacy framework.
laws.penalty: Data breach notification: civil fines per violation.
laws.exceptions: Small businesses may have reduced obligations under some state laws.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have a comprehensive consumer data privacy law?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Hawaii only has breach notification rules currently.

laws.title: Social Media Age Verification

laws.exceptions: Federal platforms regulation may preempt state laws.

laws.title: Environmental Regulations
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Environmental Code — Environmental protection
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: State environmental agency enforces air, water, and waste regulations.
laws.penalty: Environmental violations: civil fines up to $25000/day; criminal penalties for willful violations.
laws.exceptions: Some agricultural and industrial uses have specific permitting pathways.

quiz.q: Which agency enforces environmental laws in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii's state environmental agency works alongside the EPA to enforce environmental laws.

laws.title: Renewable Energy Standards
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Energy Code — Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS)
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Hawaii has the most aggressive RPS in the US — 100% renewable electricity by 2045, the first state to mandate 100% clean energy.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a policy/utility requirement, not a criminal law.
laws.exceptions: Utilities that miss RPS targets may pay alternative compliance payments.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have a Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS)?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Binding RPS requires renewable energy targets.

laws.title: Plastic Bag Laws
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §342H-78 — No statewide law
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Hawaii was the first state to ban single-use plastic bags (county-by-county, starting 2011). All counties now prohibit plastic checkout bags.
laws.penalty: Retailer violations: N/A.
laws.exceptions: Bags for meat, produce, or bulk items are often exempt.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have a statewide plastic bag ban or fee?

laws.title: Bottle Deposit Law
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §N/A — Bottle bill status
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Hawaii has a 5-cent bottle deposit on most beverage containers.
laws.penalty: Retailers not accepting returns may face fines.
laws.exceptions: Some municipal redemption centers supplement mandatory deposit systems.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have a bottle deposit/redemption law?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Hawaii has a 5-cent bottle deposit/redemption program.

laws.title: Animal Cruelty Laws
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Criminal Code — Animal cruelty prohibition
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii prohibits cruelty to animals including torture, beating, neglect, and fighting. Animal cruelty is a felony; neglect is a misdemeanor.
laws.penalty: Intentional cruelty: felony (up to 5 years). Neglect: misdemeanor (up to 1 year).
laws.exceptions: Lawful hunting, fishing, pest control, and veterinary procedures are exempt.

quiz.q: What is the maximum penalty for intentional animal cruelty in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Intentional animal cruelty is punishable by felony (up to 5 years).

laws.title: Exotic Pet Ownership

laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Dangerous exotic animals are generally prohibited as pets.

quiz.q: Are large exotic cats (lions, tigers) legal as pets in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Large exotic cats banned as pets.

laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Fire Safety Code — Consumer fireworks regulations
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Consumer fireworks regulated with some restrictions.

quiz.q: Are consumer aerial fireworks legal in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Safe-and-sane fireworks generally allowed.

laws.title: Gambling Laws
laws.subtitle: Haw. Rev. Stat. §Gaming Code — Gambling regulations
laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Hawaii is one of only two states (along with Utah) that prohibit virtually all forms of gambling. No casinos, no lottery, no sports betting.
laws.penalty: Illegal gambling: Illegal gambling: misdemeanor..
laws.exceptions: Charitable gaming (bingo, pull tabs) for nonprofits typically permitted with license.

quiz.q: Are commercial casinos legal in Hawaii?
quiz.explanation: Hawaii: Hawaii prohibits virtually all gambling — one of only two states with no lottery.

quiz.q: Does Hawaii have a right-to-repair law?

laws.fullDescription: Hawaii: Hawaii has explicitly prohibited employment discrimination based on sexual orientation since 1991, making it a pioneer in LGBTQ+ workplace rights.
laws.penalty: Employment discrimination based on LGBTQ+ status: same remedies as other protected classes.
